paper.title: AGrail: A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection
paper.central_claim: AGrail is a lifelong agent guardrail that adaptively generates and optimizes safety checks through a two-LLM (Analyzer/Executor) test-time-adaptation memory with optional tools, achieving strong ASR/benign trade-offs on task-specific and systemic risks and transferring across tasks.

evidence.quote: we propose AGrail , a lifelong agent guardrail to enhance LLM agent safety, which features adaptive safety check generation, effective safety check optimization, and tool compatibility & flexibility.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: lifelong guardrail with adaptive check generation, optimization, tool use.

evidence.quote: GuardAgent Xiang et al. (2024) struggles to address dynamic downstream tasks, as it operates under a manually specified trusted context.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 1: nearest neighbor GuardAgent depends on a manually specified trusted context.

evidence.quote: but these LLMs may misinterpret task requirements, leading to either overly restrictive policies that block legitimate actions or overly permissive ones that allow unsafe actions.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 2: LLM-generated policies (Conseca) are over/under restrictive.

evidence.quote: The Executor then evaluates the safety check from the Analyzer, deciding whether to delete it if redundant, incorrect or block legitimate agent action, and invoke external tools for validation of safety checks, or rely on self-reasoning to process it.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention gate is the Executor LLM's judgement, optionally tool-validated.

evidence.quote: allowing the framework to refine safety checks iteratively as similar agent actions are encountered.
evidence.support_explanation: Persisted memory is refined as similar actions recur.

evidence.quote: realizing a lifelong self-adaptation paradigm.
evidence.support_explanation: Convergence to the ideal check set is stated as 'ideally', without argument.

evidence.quote: If the analyzer returns in_memory as True , or if the similarity between the agent action generated by the analyzer and the original agent action in memory exceeds 0.8 , the original agent action in memory will be overwritten.
evidence.support_explanation: Write rule: overwrite the stored entry when analyzer says in_memory or similarity > 0.8; no versioning or rollback described.

evidence.quote: For AGrail, which is evaluated during TTA setting in the main experiment, we configure task-specific safety criteria aligned with guard requests from Mind2Web-SC and EICU-AC
evidence.support_explanation: Main-table AGrail numbers are test-time-adaptation numbers: memory updates while the evaluation stream is processed.

evidence.quote: In the In-Distribution (ID) setting, we split the Mind2Web-SC dataset into a training set and a test set with an 8:2 ratio.
evidence.support_explanation: ID train/test split exists for the memory ablation (Mind2Web-SC only).

evidence.quote: In Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) setting, we split the Mind2Web-SC dataset based on domains with a 3:1 ratio for training and test sets and conduct experiments in three random seeds.
evidence.support_explanation: Domain-level OOD split with three seeds.

evidence.quote: ID Claude-3.5-Sonnet 95.6 96.5 99.1 GPT-4o-mini 67.9 70.9 84.1 OOD Claude-3.5-Sonnet 89.7 93.9 94.6 GPT-4o-mini 65.9 68.0 77.8
evidence.support_explanation: No-memory / freeze-memory / TTA accuracy on Mind2Web-SC.
Claude OOD: frozen memory 93.9±1.0 vs no memory 89.7±1.0 (3 seeds).
Claude ID: frozen memory 96.5±2.4 vs no memory 95.6±1.3, within noise.
Systemic-risk results of AGrail (TTA, single reported run).
Same-foundation-model prompt baselines over-block benign actions (Norm 50-52) on Safe-OS.
Input-order sensitivity over 3 seeds: stable for Claude, large for GPT-4o-mini.

evidence.quote: our method, based on GPT-4o, had some bypassed data within the first 30 steps, but after that, the ASR dropped to 0%.
evidence.support_explanation: Learning-phase failures are admitted (AdvWeb).

evidence.quote: our token consumption falls between that of GuardAgent and the GPT-4o baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost is stated qualitatively for a figure (Figure 19, no numbers in pinned text).

evidence.quote: First, our current framework aims to explore the ability of existing LLMs to guardrail the agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Limitations section covers only off-the-shelf LLM use and scarce tools.

evidence.quote: For datasets including Safe-OS, AdvWeb, and EIA, we used Claude-3.5-Sonnet to compute agreement rates
evidence.support_explanation: Agreement metric is LLM-judged by Claude-3.5-Sonnet, also one of AGrail's foundation models.

evidence.quote: Our Safe-OS consists of 100 data, including 30 data in system sabotage attacks
evidence.support_explanation: Author-built benchmark of 100 items (30/27/20/23 by type).

evidence.quote: To ensure a fair ASR calculation, we excluded these samples from our ASR evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: ASR denominators exclude cases where the OS agent already refused (explicit, but shrinks denominators).

evidence.quote: although our ASR was marginally higher (8.8%) compared to the baseline (5.0%)
evidence.support_explanation: On AdvWeb, GPT-4o-based AGrail ASR 8.8 vs 5.0 for the GPT-4o 0-shot baseline.

evidence.quote: during TTA iterations on only one complex or simple action.
evidence.support_explanation: Convergence-to-ground-truth analysis is on a single action type with noise-initialized memory.

evidence.quote: when AGrail leverages Claude-3.5-sonnet as the foundation model, there is no performance degradation across all metrics.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory transfer Mind2Web-SC -> EICU-AC (100 samples, TTA continued).

evidence.quote: model-based defenses perform well in specific tasks but may block 49.2% of benign actions in Safe-OS
evidence.support_explanation: Real residue: prompt-only guardrails over-block benign actions.

evidence.quote: AGrail consistently ranks second across specific tasks
evidence.support_explanation: On task-specific benchmarks AGrail is not the best system by its own account.

evidence.quote: Notably, tool invocation is governed by safety checks, dynamically utillized by Executor itself.
evidence.support_explanation: Tools are invoked per safety check by the Executor.

evidence.quote: we apply a step-back prompting Zheng et al. (2024b) technique to convert the agent action into both natural language and tool command language.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory key = step-back paraphrase of the action.

evidence.quote: applying the universal safety criteria resulted in only a 2.7% decrease in accuracy.
evidence.support_explanation: Universal vs task-specific criteria trade-off.

evidence.quote: We have also validated that red-team attacks, prompt injection attacks, and environment attacks achieve at least a 90% ASR on GPT-4-turbo.
evidence.support_explanation: Attack validity check of Safe-OS.

evidence.quote: we employ an LLM as a code generator to produce a Python program that detects the environment, which is then executed within the OS agent interaction environment to obtain detection results.
evidence.support_explanation: OS tool is LLM-written code executed in the environment (real environmental feedback for environment attacks).

evidence.quote: Under the ID and OOD setting, we further evaluate the performance during TTA and found that it also outperforms the setting without memory
evidence.support_explanation: TTA online numbers beat no-memory; these are on the evaluation stream itself.

evidence.quote: In contrast, GPT-4o-mini exhibits significant variability, where both metrics fluctuate more widely.
evidence.support_explanation: Weaker backbone is order-unstable.

signatures.object: memory of per-action safety-check lists (keys: step-back paraphrase of agent action; values: safety categories + checks)
signatures.information: agent action (+ optional environment observation), user request, agent spec, guard request / safety criteria, retrieved memory entry, toolbox; ground-truth safe/unsafe labels are not stated as part of the update loop (our_inference)
signatures.operation: Analyzer retrieves entry by key, revises/merges/adds checks; Executor deletes redundant/incorrect/over-blocking checks, validates remaining ones by tool or reasoning; any Unsafe result blocks the action; entry written back
signatures.output: updated memory m(t+1) and Safe/Unsafe verdict
signatures.conditions: TTA over a stream of agent actions; frozen-memory mode after training split
signatures.feedback: Executor LLM judgement plus tool outputs (OS environment code, permission checker, HTML detector)
signatures.selection_rule: Executor decides keep/delete; overwrite of existing entry if in_memory flag or key similarity > 0.8
signatures.persistence: memory dictionary persisted across actions (TTA) or frozen after training
signatures.later_use: retrieved by key for later similar actions
signatures.claimed_effect: lower ASR with preserved benign accuracy on Safe-OS/AdvWeb/EIA; competitive on Mind2Web-SC/EICU-AC; transfer across tasks
signatures.failure_boundary: weak backbone unstable to order; learning phase misses early attacks; universal criteria cost 2.7% accuracy

signatures.object: per-check routing between Executor reasoning and external detection tools
signatures.information: safety check text, environment access, tool descriptions
signatures.operation: Executor decides per check whether to invoke OS/permission/HTML tool or reason; tool results join the verdict
signatures.conditions: tools exist for the environment (OS, EHR, EIA HTML)
signatures.persistence: tool definitions fixed; checks that need tools stay in memory
signatures.claimed_effect: catches environment-dependent attacks such as overwrite on rename

gap.author_gap: (1) adaptive risk detection across tasks (GuardAgent relies on a manual trusted context); (2) effective safety policies (LLM-generated policies/CoT guardrails are over- or under-restrictive)
gap.checked_gap: Residue is real in the paper's own data (prompt-only guardrails block ~50% benign actions on Safe-OS), and the fixed object is named (manually specified checks). claims.text: Strong performance against systemic risks with preserved benign actions (e.g., 0% ASR on prompt injection, 3.8%/5% on sabotage/environment)
claims.setting: Safe-OS, AdvWeb, EIA; Claude-3.5 / GPT-4o backbones
claims.baseline_control: same-LLM 0/1-shot prompt guardrails, AgentMonitor, LLaMA-Guard3, ToolEmu
claims.selection_vs_test: online TTA on the evaluated stream
claims.result_denominator: Safe-OS 100 items; ASR denominators exclude agent self-refusals; single run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under online adaptation on small author-built sets, AGrail blocks attacks while over-blocking far less than same-LLM prompt guardrails; not a held-out generalization result.

claims.selection_vs_test: memory built on train split then frozen on test split (FM)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Frozen memory helps clearly only in Claude OOD on one dataset; other gains are within seed noise.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A memory of safety checks built on a Mind2Web-SC training split and frozen improves held-out accuracy for Claude (OOD +4.2 points), and online TTA numbers on Safe-OS/AdvWeb/EIA show far lower benign over-blocking than same-LLM prompt guardrails with low ASR; held-out, seed-robust and budget-matched evidence beyond Mind2Web-SC is absent.

G.reason: Names a fixed component (manually specified trusted contexts / checks), nearest neighbors, and a measurable residue (benign over-blocking up to 49%); neighbors' originals unverified and residual limits only partly stated.

M.reason: Concrete mechanism (Analyzer/Executor, step-back key, per-check tools) fits the over-blocking problem, but edits are driven by LLM self-judgement with no obtainable outcome label, and the 'converges to ideal check set' objective is unobservable.

X.reason: Algorithms, key construction, overwrite threshold and tool roles are given; prompts are figures not in the pinned text, how memory is 'trained' (labels?) is unstated, and no versioning, rollback, forgetting or growth control.

E.measurement.reason: Standard classification/ASR metrics with attack validity checked, but author-built 100-item Safe-OS, ASR excludes self-refusals, and the agreement metric is LLM-judged by a model that is also an evaluated backbone.

E.causality.reason: Memory ablation (no/freeze/TTA, 3 seeds, 2 backbones) isolates the stored checks on Mind2Web-SC; no Executor-off, tool-off, append-only or nearest-neighbor controls and none on Safe-OS; system-level baselines are single-call.

E.holdout.reason: Mind2Web-SC ID/OOD splits give a clean freeze-memory test, but all main-table and transfer numbers are online TTA on the evaluated stream and the benchmark is authored with the method; no overlap analysis.

E.statistics.reason: Three-seed std for memory and order ablations, learning-phase failures disclosed; main tables are single runs on 20-100 item groups with no intervals.

E.cost.reason: Cost is only a qualitative token comparison (figure) with no counts, latency or tool-codegen cost despite two LLM calls plus tools per action.

rationale: Memory of safety checks helps on Mind2Web-SC (frozen, 3 seeds); main numbers are online TTA on small author-built sets; gate and tools unablated.
